facts.statement: Orthosuchus lived during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages of the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Hettangian-Sinemurian

facts.statement: The species Orthosuchus stormbergi was named by Nash in 1968.
facts.quote: authority: Nash, 1968

facts.statement: Orthosuchus was first discovered in 1963 in the Red Beds Formation of the Qacha's Nek Province in Lesotho.
facts.quote: It was first discovered in 1963 in the Red Beds Formation in the Qacha's Nek Province of Lesotho, southern Africa.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodyliforms meaning "straight crocodile".
facts.quote: Orthosuchus (meaning "straight crocodile") is an extinct genus of crocodyliform

facts.statement: Orthosuchus had a body length of about 60 to 70 centimeters and a body proportion similar to lizards.
facts.quote: Orthosuchus has a body proportion similar to lizards, with a body length about 60 - 70 cm

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Orthosuchus likely held 15 to 18 teeth of equal size and similar shape.
facts.quote: The dentary forms the largest part of the lower jaw with some shallow pits, which indicated that the animal probably has 15-18 teeth

facts.statement: Orthosuchus possessed 24 vertebrae, with 8 located in the neck region.
facts.quote: Orthosuchus has 24 vertebrae, and 8 of them are believed to be in the cervical region.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus had five digits on its limbs.
facts.quote: Orthosuchus appeared to have 5 digits.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus had earflaps that protected its ears from water when swimming.
facts.quote: The ears are protected by earflaps, which prevent water inflow to the otic recess when this animal is in water.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus is closely related to Protosuchus, Notochampsa, and Erythrochampsa.
facts.quote: Orthosuchus is closely related to Protosuchus, Notochampsa, Erythrochampsa, and probably other crocodilian families.

facts.statement: A 2021 revision placed Orthosuchus as the sister taxon to Notochampsa within the family Notochampsidae.
facts.quote: A revision of Notochampsa in 2021 found it valid taxon, and phylogenetic analysis recovered it as sister to Orthosuchus, in a monophyletic Notochampsidae.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus had a small salt-secreting gland, indicating it was not a marine animal.
facts.quote: Orthosuchus has a small salt-secreting gland, which indicates that it is not a marine animal.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus was probably quadrupedal because its forelimbs were about 91% the length of its hind limbs.
facts.quote: The animal is probably quadrupedal because the fore limbs are approximately 91% the length of the hind limb

facts.statement: Unlike modern crocodiles, Orthosuchus likely walked upright with its femur vertical to the ground rather than creeping on its belly.
facts.quote: Unlike modern crocodiles, Orthosuchus does not creep on its belly; it probably walks at a high position with its femur vertical to the ground.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Orthosuchus may have hunted by slowly approaching schools of small fish and striking from the side.
facts.quote: It is possible that Orthosuchus has the same predation, by slowly moving toward schools of small fish and swallow from the side.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Orthosuchus belongs to the family Protosuchidae, though it shares characteristics with that group.
facts.quote: The classification of Protosuchidae is debatable, however, since Orthosuchus resemble some of the characteristics of Protosuchidae, it is believed to be in the part of this family.

facts.statement: Orthosuchus may not have been a good swimmer because its amphicoelous vertebrae lacked the tail mobility found in modern crocodiles.
facts.quote: However, Orthosuchus may not be a good swimmer, since it has amphicoelous vertebrae, whereas modern crocodiles have procoelous vertebrae, which increase the mobility of the tail.

facts.statement: The genus Orthosuchus was named by Nash in 1968.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Orthosuchus (genus), Nash 1968

facts.statement: Orthosuchus belongs to the family Notochampsidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Notochampsidae

facts.statement: Orthosuchus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Orthosuchus lived between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago during the Hettangian to Sinemurian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Orthosuchus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
